A Cashless Society and the Implication for Preppers

Sadly the author uses future tense of most words, the reality is that all they things he warns could happen are long since here. Everything we do is tracked and parsed and cross referenced and recorded. Everything. Spending cash and talking in person ( out of sight of cameras and away from electronic devices like phones and tvs) are the only freedom we have left.
New to the whole prepper thing, is cash really that useful even? In a survival situation.

Most of prepping should be geared for mad max or zombie apocalypse. There are plenty of shades of calamity in between ranging from list job to nuclear emp. The goal for most is to prepare for anything. Sticking back cash could help if I net services were down for any reason in an area, or if your identity was compromised from a hack, or even if you want to buy things in such a way that you do not leave an electronic trail. Storing s chunk of cash should definitely be a priority. For any scenario you still need the same things: food, water, shelter, security and information/communication. Consider scenarios from higher likelihood to lower likelihood and make sure you are prepared to meet those needs as efficiently as possible. In most cases there is a great deal of overlap, but any preparedness is better than none.
That's a good point. I've always thought of preppers as full-blown guerilla warfare living out in the woods. But maybe that's a very narrow viewpoint of the entire spectrum.
